fact: The East African Policy Observer, drawing on the Carnegie Endowment's Africa Technology Policy Tracker, says Rwanda's binding legal instruments include cybersecurity law and that all three countries reviewed, Rwanda among them, have cybersecurity laws; no date is given for the statement, so the document's published date is used.
Rwanda's Supreme Court on 5 June 2025 upheld the constitutionality of Article 39 of the 2018 Cybercrime Law, which criminalises publishing rumours through digital platforms, per CIVICUS Monitor.
Digital Policy Alert says the 2018 Law on the Prevention and Punishment of Cyber Crimes is Rwanda's main cybersecurity framework and criminalises unauthorised access and data interception.
